note: BJT business vocabulary (target BJT 400+, J3/J2 boundary). Every item is verified: single words and set expressions against JMdict/EDRDG (scripts/verify_jmdict.js: exact written form + primary reading, senses recorded in sources); phrases by real usage (Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR) and, for keigo forms it covers, 文化審議会答申「敬語の指針」(2007). Example sentences marked "constructed": true were written for this app; others are the cited Tatoeba sentences. tier: 1 essential for 400 / 2 useful / 3 stretch. register: neutral | polite | honorific (尊敬語) | humble (謙譲語) | formal-written | casual. pair: id of a confusable item or the opposite-direction keigo form.

items.note: Formal meeting with an agenda (定例会議 regular meeting, 会議に出る/出席する). For a smaller working session with a client or colleague, 打ち合わせ is more usual.

example.jp: 午後の会議は3時からです。
example.en: This afternoon's meeting starts at 3.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: meeting; conference; session; assembly; council; convention; congress

items.note: The everyday word for a working meeting or discussion to settle details, internal or with a client: 打ち合わせをする, 打ち合わせの日程. Less formal than 会議.

example.jp: 来週、先方と打ち合わせをします。
example.en: We have a meeting with the client next week.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
sources.matched: 打ち合わせ【うちあわせ】

items.note: Item on the agenda: 次の議題に移ります "let's move to the next item". 議題に上げる = put on the agenda.

example.jp: 本日の議題は三つあります。
example.en: There are three items on today's agenda.

items.note: Handouts, slides, reference documents: 資料を配る, 会議資料, 資料をお送りします. A very frequent word in BJT emails and meetings.

example.jp: 明日の会議の資料を準備しておいてください。
example.en: Please get the materials ready for tomorrow's meeting.

items.note: Attending a meeting or event: 会議に出席する. Polite request: ご出席ください. Opposite: 欠席.

example.jp: 部長も会議に出席されます。
example.en: The department manager will also attend the meeting.

items.note: Not attending: 会議を欠席する. When you will miss a meeting, report it in advance: 欠席させていただきます.

example.jp: 体調不良のため、本日の会議を欠席します。
example.en: I will miss today's meeting because I am unwell.

items.note: 結論が出る (a conclusion is reached), 結論を出す. In reports, put the conclusion first: 結論から申し上げますと…

example.jp: 今日の会議では結論が出ませんでした。
example.en: We did not reach a conclusion at today's meeting.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: conclusion (of an argument, discussion, study, etc.)

items.note: Meeting room; often numbered or named: 第一会議室. 会議室を予約する = book a meeting room.

example.jp: 会議室を10時から予約しました。
example.en: I booked the meeting room from 10 o'clock.

items.note: Written record of a meeting; typically the junior person 議事録を取る/作成する and circulates it afterwards.

example.jp: 会議の議事録を皆さんに送ります。
example.en: I will send everyone the minutes of the meeting.

items.note: Speaking up in a meeting: 発言する, 発言を求める. 発言者 = the speaker.

example.jp: 何かご意見があれば、自由に発言してください。
example.en: If you have any opinions, please feel free to speak.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: statement; remark; observation; utterance; speech; proposal

items.note: The dates/timetable of an event or meeting: 日程を調整する (find a date that suits everyone), 日程が決まる. Compare 予定 (one person's plans).

example.jp: 打ち合わせの日程を調整させてください。
example.en: Please let me arrange the dates for the meeting.

items.note: A plan or what is scheduled: 予定がある, 〜する予定です. Compare 日程 (dates of an event) and 予約 (a booking).

example.jp: 来週の月曜日は出張の予定です。
example.en: I am scheduled to be on a business trip next Monday.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: plans; arrangement; schedule; program; programme; expectation; estimate

items.note: Whether a time suits someone: ご都合はいかがですか (asking a client), 都合がつく / 都合が悪い. 都合により = for reasons of convenience (vague reason in notices).

example.jp: 木曜日のご都合はいかがでしょうか。
example.en: Would Thursday suit you?

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: in all; in total; all told

items.note: Short for アポイントメント: an appointment with a client. アポを取る = make an appointment. Casual-neutral office jargon; in writing to clients use お約束.

example.jp: 来週、新しいお客様とのアポを取りました。
example.en: I made an appointment with a new customer for next week.

items.note: Adjusting to make things fit: 日程調整 (finding a date), 予算を調整する. Also used as a soft way to say something is still being arranged: 現在調整中です.

example.jp: 会議の時間は現在調整中です。
example.en: The meeting time is currently being arranged.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: adjustment; regulation; coordination; reconciliation; tuning; fixing; tailoring

items.note: Cut-off time for submitting something (applications, reports): 締め切りに間に合う / 遅れる. Compare 期限 (validity period/time limit in general) and 納期 (delivery date).

example.jp: 報告書の締め切りは金曜日です。
example.en: The deadline for the report is Friday.

items.note: During the morning (until noon): 午前中に送ります = I will send it by/within the morning.

example.jp: 資料は明日の午前中にお送りします。
example.en: I will send the materials tomorrow morning.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: in the morning; during the morning

items.note: Formal word for 今日, standard on the phone, in notices and announcements: 本日はありがとうございました.

example.jp: 本日は、お忙しいところありがとうございました。
example.en: Thank you very much for your time today.

items.en: the other day; a few days ago
items.note: A few days ago; standard in business openers: 先日はありがとうございました (thanks for the other day).

example.en: Thank you for your time the other day.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: the other day; a few days ago

items.note: As soon as possible; marks urgency on requests: 至急ご連絡ください, 【至急】 in an email subject.

example.jp: 至急、確認をお願いします。
example.en: Please check this urgently.

example.en: We will contact you later with the details.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API

items.note: Urgent, prompt (often 早急に対応します). JMdict lists そうきゅう first; さっきゅう is the traditional reading and both are heard. More formal than 急いで; compare 至急.

example.jp: 早急に原因を調べます。
example.en: We will investigate the cause promptly.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: immediate; prompt; quick; rapid; urgent; pressing
pos: Noun which may take the genitive case particle 'no'

items.note: Telling your superior about results or progress: 上司に報告する. Part of 報連相.

example.jp: 結果を課長に報告しました。
example.en: I reported the results to the section manager.

items.note: Getting in touch, passing information: 連絡する, ご連絡ください, 連絡先 (contact details). Part of 報連相.

example.jp: 何かあれば、すぐに連絡してください。
example.en: If anything happens, contact me right away.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API

connection (with a train, bus, etc.); joining (a railway line, etc.); meeting

items.note: Asking for advice or discussing before deciding: 上司に相談する, ご相談があるのですが.

example.jp: この件について、少しご相談したいことがあります。
example.en: There is something about this matter I would like to discuss with you.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: consultation; discussion; discussing; asking (someone) for advice

items.note: Current situation: 状況を確認する, 現在の状況, 進捗状況.

example.jp: 現在の状況を教えていただけますか。
example.en: Could you tell me the current situation?

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: state of affairs; situation; conditions; circumstances

items.note: Checking/confirming: 確認する, ご確認ください, 念のため確認させてください. One of the most frequent business words.

example.jp: 日時をもう一度確認させてください。
example.en: Let me confirm the date and time once more.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: confirmation; verification; validation; review; check; affirmation; identification

items.note: Details: 詳細を確認する, 詳細は添付ファイルをご覧ください.

example.jp: 詳細は添付ファイルをご確認ください。
example.en: Please see the attached file for details.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: close-up view (of a digitally displayed map); zoomed-in view

items.note: A matter or case: この件, 先日の件, 〜の件で (about ~). Used constantly in email subjects and phone calls.

example.jp: 先日の見積もりの件でお電話しました。
example.en: I am calling about the estimate from the other day.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API

items.en: being in charge (of an area of responsibility)
items.note: Being responsible for something: 〜を担当する, 担当の者 (the person in charge, humble), ご担当 (the client's person in charge).

example.en: I am in charge of sales.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: person in charge (of an area of work, etc.); person responsible; contact (person)

items.note: Progress of work: 進捗状況 (progress status), 進捗を報告する. Very common in project meetings.

example.jp: 毎週、進捗を報告してください。
example.en: Please report your progress every week.

items.note: Sharing information or files with a team: 情報を共有する, 共有フォルダ.

example.jp: この情報はチーム全員で共有しましょう。
example.en: Let's share this information with the whole team.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API

items.note: 報告・連絡・相談: the classic Japanese workplace rule to report, keep people informed and consult. Sounds like ほうれん草 (spinach).

example.jp: 新入社員は報連相を大切にしてください。
example.en: New employees should take reporting, informing and consulting seriously.

items.note: Handing work over to a successor or the next shift: 引き継ぎをする, 引き継ぎ資料. Verb: 引き継ぐ.

example.jp: 異動の前に、後任に仕事の引き継ぎをします。
example.en: Before the transfer, I will hand my work over to my successor.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API

items.note: A proposal: 提案する, ご提案, 新しい提案をまとめる.

example.jp: 新しい販売方法を提案したいと思います。
example.en: I would like to propose a new sales method.

items.note: Planning a project or event: 企画を立てる, 企画部 (planning department).

example.jp: 来年のイベントの企画を立てています。
example.en: I am planning next year's event.

items.note: A request or commission (formal noun): 依頼する, ご依頼, 依頼書. In conversation お願い is more common.

example.jp: お客様から見積もりの依頼がありました。
example.en: A customer asked for an estimate.

items.note: Approval by someone with authority: 上司の承認を得る, 承認が下りる.

example.jp: この計画には部長の承認が必要です。
example.en: This plan needs the department manager's approval.

sources.name: JMdict/EDRDG via jisho.org API
senses: recognition; acknowledgement; acknowledgment; approval; consent; agreement

items.note: Cooperation: ご協力をお願いします (standard in notices), 協力会社 (partner company).
